title: Loop and Iteration
definition: A loop repeatedly executes a defined body while its continuation rule permits another iteration.
purpose: Express finite or condition-controlled repetition without duplicating instructions.
history: Sequence, selection, and iteration are foundational structured-programming control forms.
mental_model: A program returns to a checkpoint, asks whether another round is allowed, executes one round, updates state, and asks again.
analogy: Walking repeated laps models iteration; it fails when an iteration can skip work, exit early, or mutate several pieces of state.
industry_notes: Choose a loop form that makes the source of repetition, progress, and exit visible rather than merely minimizing syntax.
ai_notes: AI often produces plausible loops without an explicit termination argument or boundary trace.
interview_notes: Ask for initialization-condition-body-update order and an iteration table.
